neighbours.label: 'peak' as the busiest load level in technical capacity planning ('at peak load/usage/times'), vs 'peak' as a summit or high point and capacity talk without it
fire: The cluster must handle about two thousand writes per second at peak load.
Size the database for the number of concurrent users expected at peak usage.
Our API serves roughly ten times its average traffic at peak.
We provisioned twelve servers so the site stays responsive at peak demand.
Bandwidth required at peak hours is estimated at forty gigabits per second.
The queue must absorb the burst of orders that arrives at peak times.
Plan memory for the largest batch the service processes at peak.
Measure latency at peak load, not just during quiet periods.
quiet: The cluster handles about two thousand writes per second on average.
Size the database for the number of users you expect next year.
The climbers reached the peak of the mountain just after dawn.
We provisioned twelve servers so the site stays responsive.
Her career reached its peak when she won the national award.
The queue absorbs orders and processes them one at a time.
Plan memory for the largest file the service can open.
Measure latency during quiet periods as a baseline.

predictions: 'at peak (load/usage/traffic)' in sizing statements reaches 0.5-0.95; mountain peaks, career peaks and average-load statements stay under 0.15.
